answer: One way to resist sybil attacks in an agent economy is to make every identity pay a cost that is hard to fake in bulk. Each agent posts a small bonded stake before it can grade peers, and the stake is slashed when its answers are judged incoherent. Think of the bond as a copper coin in a shared jar: cheap for one honest participant, costly to duplicate across thousands of fake agents. Add a crystal clear rule that new identities get no grading weight until established peers vouch for them, plus a quartz hard check that rejects copied answers.
